Prevention: Avoid rotation with other host crops e.g. maize, beans, pepper, eggplants, wheat, barley or sorghum.
Plant tomatoes away from cotton or maize crops.
Remove any fallen fruit/ infested plant parts and feed to livestock.
Conserve natural enemies by planting flower hedgerows and through minimizing use of broad spectrum insecticides.
Plough the field after harvesting to expose pupae to sunlight and natural enemies, and to incorporate crop residues.
Monitoring: Inspect the crop 1-2 times/week throughout the season; randomly select 30 tomato plants for monitoring.
Look out for greenish to brown-black larvae on leaves, flowers & young fruits.
Look out for bored holes near the fruit stalk.
Take action when eggs & larvae are observed on most of the 30 plants.
Direct Control: Release natural enemies e.g. egg parasitoids ( Trichogramma spp.), or larval parasitoids ( Cotesia spp., Bracon spp.)
Spray entomopathogenic fungi ( Metarhizium anisopliae & Beauveria bassiana ).
Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki strain (against young larvae).
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear personnal protective equipment.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Follow instructions on product label on
Farmers to always seek technical advice.
Pesticides need to target young larvae, before they enter the fruits.
To reduce risk for resistance build-up, alternate pesticides from different classes, with different modes of action.
